chunks: Say: 'Are you waiting for anything else but one of two good things for us, (victory or martyrdom)? Yet what we are waiting for you is the punishment of God, direct or through us. So keep waiting; we are waiting with you.'

key_terms.إِحْدَى الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ: one of the two good things (victory or martyrdom)

ai.seo_question: What are the two good things Muslims expected from the Battle of Badr according to Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a reassurance to the Prophet and the believers during the period of waiting for divine decree, emphasizing that 'the two goods' refer to victory in this world or martyrdom in the hereafter. It underscores the concept of *tawakkul* (trust in God) amidst the uncertainty of battle, contrasting the disbelievers' impatience with the believers' steadfast expectation of God's justice. The phrase 'or through us' highlights the agency granted to the faithful as instruments of divine punishment, a theme central to the narrative of the Conquest of Mecca.
